conversations.title: Lunch at Sakurazaka Park
conversations.note: Japanese people often say お疲れさま to coworkers or friends during the day, not only at the end of work. Adding ね to the end of a sentence, as in 高いね, invites the listener to agree and keeps talk friendly.

lines.ja: 怜奈さん、お疲れさま！今日、給料日なんだ。
lines.en: Hi Rena, good work! Today's payday, you know.

lines.ja: お疲れ。テンション高いね。何かいいことあったの？
lines.en: Hey. You're really hyped. Did something good happen?

lines.ja: あのね、昨日のお客さんが深夜のラーメン聞いてきたの。
lines.en: So, a guest yesterday asked me for a good late-night ramen spot.

lines.ja: また人のごはんの話？ほんと気になるんだね。
lines.en: Back to other people's food again? You really are curious.

lines.ja: だって気になるじゃん！六本木のお店、教えてあげた。
lines.en: Well, I'm curious! I told them about a place in Roppongi.

lines.ja: 優しいね。じゃあ、お昼どうする？時間あんまりないよ。
lines.en: That's nice of you. So, lunch? We don't have much time.

lines.ja: わかばどう？近いし、ランチセットがすぐ出るよ。
lines.en: How about Wakaba? It's close and the lunch set comes out fast.

lines.ja: いいね。じゃあ、わかばにしよう。
lines.en: Sounds good. Let's go to Wakaba then.

ending.because: Yui and Rena both work close to Roppongi, so Wakaba is an easy walk from either workplace. Its quick lunch set fits their short break.

there.ja: すみません、ランチセットふたつお願いします。
there.en: Excuse me, two lunch sets please.

there.ja: 私は唐揚げ定食にする。あと、お水もね。
there.en: I'll have the karaage set. And water too, please.

there.ja: 私も同じのにしよう。今日は割り勘でいい？
there.en: I'll get the same one. Shall we split the bill today?

there.ja: えー、給料日なのにおごってくれないの？
there.en: Eh, it's payday and you won't treat me?

there.ja: 半分だけね！ちょっとだけだよ。
there.en: Half only! Just a little, okay.

there.ja: はいはい。ありがとう、ゆいちゃん。

conversations.title: Sakurazaka Park Meetup
conversations.note: Coworkers say お疲れさま to each other when they meet after work, even in casual settings. Shota's ね and じゃん and Rena's blunt replies show how Tokyo friends often tease each other while still being warm.

lines.ja: おー、みんな来た！今日めっちゃ疲れたわー。
lines.en: Oh, everyone's here! I'm so tired today.

lines.ja: お疲れさま！ねえ聞いて、今日のお客さんがおもしろくて。
lines.en: Good work! Listen, the guest today was so funny.

lines.ja: また始まった。
lines.en: Here we go again.

lines.ja: 亮、昼に何食べたか言ってみ？
lines.en: Ryo, tell us what you ate for lunch.

lines.ja: ……カレーです。
lines.en: ...Curry.

lines.ja: カレー！？まじで？寝ぼけてんじゃん。
lines.en: Curry?! Seriously? You must have been half asleep.

lines.ja: 別にいいでしょ。おいしかったです。
lines.en: What's wrong with that? It was good.

lines.ja: 亮くんのカレーはどうでもいいけど、お腹すいた。
lines.en: I don't care about Ryo's curry, but I'm hungry.

lines.ja: わかる。で、そのお客さんがね、ロビーで…
lines.en: Me too. So, that guest, in the lobby...

lines.ja: 長くなりそう。居酒屋行きながら聞こうか。
lines.en: Sounds like a long story. Let's go somewhere to eat while you tell it.

lines.ja: じゃあ、たいとでよくない？近いし焼き鳥うまいよ！
lines.en: Then how about Taito? It's close and the yakitori is great!

lines.ja: いいね！賛成！
lines.en: Nice! I agree!

lines.ja: 私もいい。
lines.en: Fine with me too.

lines.ja: ……あの、入口から遠い席がいいです。
lines.en: ...Um, I'd like a seat far from the entrance.

lines.ja: 亮、また人見知りかよ（笑）。
lines.en: Ryo, you're shy again, huh? (lol)

lines.ja: じゃ、たいとに行こ。
lines.en: Okay, let's go to Taito.

ending.because: They meet near Sakurazaka Park after work. Shota suggests Taito because it is close and has good yakitori, and everyone agrees. Ryo asks only for a seat away from the door, so they all head there together.

there.ja: 四人です。奥の席、空いてますか？
there.en: Four of us. Is there a seat in the back?

there.ja: 焼き鳥、とりあえずもも、ねぎま、つくね頼もう！
there.en: Let's order yakitori to start: thigh, leek and chicken, and meatballs!

there.ja: 生ビールひとつ。あとレモンサワーで。
there.en: One draft beer for me. And a lemon sour after that.

there.ja: ねえ、さっきの話の続き聞いて！
there.en: Hey, listen to the rest of that story!
